attachments.insertion_landmark: posterior tubercles of the transverse processes C1-C3

actions: rotates and laterally flexes the neck to the same side

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

injection_target_points.label: centre of the region of highest muscle spindle abundance
injection_target_points.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve-dense region, with muscle-spindle abundance histology, localised by spiral CT with barium sulphate labelling
injection_target_points.notes: Deeper and further from the occiput than splenius capitis, on both reference lines.
injection_target_points.source: He X, Wen S, Liu X, Li Y, Yang S, 'Optimal target localization for botulinum toxin A in treating splenius muscles dystonia based on the distribution of intramuscular nerves and spindles', Anat Sci Int 101(1):44-53 (2025), doi:10.1007/s12565-025-00831-8 -- 24 adults, modified Sihler's staining with muscle-spindle histology and CT localisation

motor_endplate_zones.reference_line_to: posterior tubercles of the transverse processes C1-C3 (insertion)
motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's staining, intramuscular nerve arborization mapping
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Nerve pathways ran vertically from the insertion toward the origin, with motor entry concentrated over the middle 40% of muscle length. Muscle is also implicated in chronic tension-type headache. A later cadaveric CT-localization study on an independent sample narrowed the densest sub-zone further, to roughly 56-64% of muscle length -- see this muscle's injection_target_points entry for that more precise point.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Kwon HJ, Yang HM, Won SY, 'Intramuscular innervation patterns of the splenius capitis and splenius cervicis and their clinical implications for botulinum toxin injections', Clin Anat 33(8):1138-1143 (2020), doi:10.1002/ca.23553 -- 10 splenius cervicis specimens from cadaveric dissection, modified Sihler's staining. Retrieved via PubMed.

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe (5-18 MHz) over the posterior triangle of the neck at the level of the C4-C5 spinous processes; scan laterally to identify the levator scapulae muscle belly, then look immediately deep to it.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Deep to levator scapulae; at the C4-C5 level splenius cervicis is the most superficial component of the common lateral muscle mass (shared with longissimus cervicis, and with splenius capitis more cranially).
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Dynamic lateral scanning shows the muscle's downward, backward and inward fiber orientation, helping distinguish it from the adjacent longissimus cervicis. The chosen landmark was validated by placing a metal clip under ultrasound guidance and confirming its position by cadaveric dissection.
structures_at_risk: levator scapulae (deliberately transfixed en route to the target)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Injection is carried out anteroposteriorly, transfixing levator scapulae, aiming for the craniocaudal space bounded by the horizontal lines through the C4 and C5 spinous processes. Landmark defined on 2 fixed cadavers plus MRI/ultrasound correlation in a healthy volunteer, then validated on a fresh cadaver.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Brumpt E, Aubry S, Vuillier F, Tatu L, 'Anatomo-sonographic identification of the longissimus capitis and splenius cervicis muscles: principles for possible application to ultrasound-guided botulinum toxin injections in cervical dystonia', Surg Radiol Anat 43(6):909-915 (2021), doi:10.1007/s00276-020-02646-w -- 2 fixed cadavers + 1 fresh cadaver, ultrasound/MRI correlation with cadaveric dissection validation. Retrieved via PubMed.
